A micro-feature embedded inside Neema's core remittance flow — giving eligible users the ability to send money home even when their balance runs short.

Product Designer
Neema
POC / Pilot
April 2025
01

Context

Neema is a financial app built for migrant workers in Israel. Their core routine is simple: receive salary, send it home. Most users transfer nearly their entire balance every month — a deeply familiar, trusted ritual.

But life doesn't sync with payday. A school fee, a medical bill, a family emergency back home — sometimes it can't wait. Users found themselves needing to send money before their next paycheck arrived, with no way to do it.

"They needed to send money. The money wasn't there yet. We built the bridge."

₪300–1K

Loan range per transfer

30

Days to repay

6+

Months of activity required for eligibility

Who uses Send More

Eligible users — those with 6+ months of consistent sending history, monthly app activity, and a track record Neema trusts. A limited, high-quality segment.

How it works

One active loan at a time. Repayment collected automatically from balance after 30 days. If repayment fails, every deposit goes toward settling the debt.

02

The Challenge

The send money flow is the heart of Neema. It's familiar, trusted — and used by people who are resistant to change. Adding anything on top of it came with real risk: confuse users, disrupt the flow, or introduce friction into the one thing they do every month without thinking.

Don't break a flow that already works perfectly

Users are not tech-savvy and are resistant to change

The word "loan" carries weight — anxiety, hesitation, risk

"We made a deliberate choice: don't call it a loan. Call it Send More."

Framing was everything. By naming it Send More, we shifted the mental model from debt to opportunity. The user isn't taking out a loan — they're sending their family a little extra.

03

Design Decisions

We explored multiple directions before landing on the right approach. Each version taught us something about what the feature needed to feel like.

Rejected

Widget overlay

Floated on top of the existing flow. Felt like an interruption — demanding attention mid-task rather than inviting curiosity.

Rejected

Information-heavy entry

Front-loaded terms and conditions before users even understood the offer. Created anxiety before value was communicated.

Chosen

Embedded toggle + slider

Integrated directly into the amount entry screen. Appears at the natural moment of decision. Playful, opt-in, entirely ignorable.

Chosen principle

Celebratory activation

Turning on Send More triggers a small celebration — an animation that makes the action feel like a positive choice, not a financial risk.

Off — ignored
On — slider reveals

The toggle as an entry point

The toggle is the entire invitation. Off by default, zero pressure. When activated, a slider expands below — choosing the amount feels like a game, not a commitment.

The eligibility logic runs silently in the background. Only qualifying users ever see the feature — everyone else has a completely unchanged experience.

04

Send More lives inside the existing remittance flow — appearing only at the moment the user is choosing an amount, and only for eligible users.

Results

The pilot launched in April 2025 to a limited group of eligible users. Early signals indicate the feature earned genuine trust — users not only understood and adopted it, they repaid even when it wasn't strictly on time.

Key signal

Users repaid even when delayed — suggesting interest accumulation was less concerning than expected. Trust over urgency.

What's next

Measure repayment behavior at scale, validate risk assumptions, and evaluate expanding eligibility beyond the pilot group.
